blocks.text: Today we're launching spaces, a new way to interact with agents and your team in Amp.

inlines.text: Today we're launching spaces, a new way to interact with agents and your team in Amp.

blocks.text: A space is a conversation with a single agent whose job is to spawn and coordinate agents for you. You no longer have to create and organize threads yourself; the agent in a space will do it for you.

inlines.text: A space is a conversation with a single agent whose job is to spawn and coordinate agents for you. You no longer have to create and organize threads yourself; the agent in a space will do it for you.

blocks.text: It's a new, higher-level way to work with many agents.

inlines.text: It's a new, higher-level way to work with many agents.

blocks.text: After using spaces for the past few weeks, we think this might be the future of interacting with agents. There's something special about this way of working. You operate with a bird's-eye view but can still dive into the weeds when necessary. It's more like sitting in the captain's chair than down in the trenches.

blocks.text: We also found that we naturally moved into the space to communicate with each other. Instead of Slack, we found ourselves taking video calls and discussions into the space.

blocks.text: Here are some examples of how we've been using spaces at Amp.

inlines.text: Here are some examples of how we've been using spaces at Amp.

blocks.text: Spaces were built in a space. Tim, Lewis, Nicolay and the rest of the team shared one called "Spaces v1", dropped feedback, bugs and new ideas into the chat, and the agent delegated them into threads. When they needed to talk, they used comments to chat and then tagged in Amp when they were ready.

blocks.alt: The Spaces v1 space: teammates post feedback with replies under each message, the agent notes it and reports that the new Spaces icons shipped, and the side panel lists the space's threads by status.

blocks.text: Lewis ran the launch of service accounts from one space. From the space, Lewis could roll out the feature, monitor X, Slack, and bug reports for issues, fix incoming bugs, and send out emails and refunds to affected users. The space monitored user issues and system health for the rest of the week.

blocks.text: Will gave a space a goal: review recent changes for security issues. Its first run split the codebase into 16 areas, reviewed each in its own thread, checked every finding in another, and kept a summary artifact in the space for Will to review and track.

blocks.text: To start a space, use the + in the Spaces section of the sidebar, set a title and a project, and then tell your agent what to work on.
